summary: This paper demonstrates wafer-scale fabrication of high-quality Nb/Al-AlO$_x$/Nb cross-type Josephson junctions using chemical-mechanical polishing (CMP) for planarization instead of lift-off processes, achieving >90% yield and junction areas down to $1	imes1$ µm$^2$. The CMP-based process produces uniform critical current density $j_c  acksim 220$ A/cm$^2$ and resistance ratio $R_{m sg}/R_N  acksim 38$, with area-independent characteristic voltage $V_c  acksim 1.4$ mV demonstrating consistent tunnel barrier quality across the wafer.
motivation: Cross-type junction geometry offers smaller areas and eliminates parasitic capacitances compared to window-type geometries, improving DC SQUID energy sensitivity, but wafer-scale production requires reliable, reproducible processes with uniform quality across large areas.
method: Nb/Al-AlO$_x$/Nb trilayers are sputtered ($j_c$ tuned via 65 min oxidation at 33.3 mbar), patterned by optical lithography and ICP-RIE (vertical sidewalls with $P_{m HF}=30$ W, $P_{m ICP}=300$ W), embedded in sputter-deposited SiO$_2$ (nominally 500 nm), and planarized by CMP at $p_{m head}=138$ mbar and $p_{m ret}=103$ mbar with material removal rate $ acksim 128$ nm/min, yielding within-wafer uniformity of 5% and wafer-to-wafer uniformity of 1–6%.
result: Junctions scale linearly with corrected area (width correction $ acksim 0.4$–0.8 µm depending on photoresist), with gap voltage $V_{m gap}=2.84±0.03$ mV consistent with bulk Nb, subgap resistance ratio $38.3±1.5$ on wafer A and $31.2±0.8$ on wafer B, and Fraunhofer patterns indicating smooth edge-damage regions of $ acksim 800$ nm and effective Nb penetration depth $ acksim 84$ nm.
